blurb: Comparisons (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) and equality tests (`==`, `!=`) do not chain, so `a < b < c` is refused rather than given a reading you may not have meant. Split a chain of comparisons with `&&`; to test the result of an equality, parenthesise it: `(a == b) == c`.
summary: A non-associative operator was chained (e.g. `a == b == c`).
